<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>

The `makepkg --printsrcinfo` command only reads and parses the PKGBUILD file itself—it does not execute any of the functions defined in the file (such as `build()`, `package_backintime_cli()`, or `package_backintime`). Since `makepkg --printsrcinfo` operates at the parsing stage and does not invoke the build or installation steps, none of the top-level code, variable assignments, or source declarations are executed during this operation. There are no command substitutions, shell invocations, or external payloads being triggered. The only action taken is reading the file content to extract metadata (variables, source URLs, checksums, etc.), which is inherently safe.

All the actual functionality in this PKGBUILD—including the `build()` function that runs configure/make and the `package_backintime_cli()`/`package_backintime()` functions that handle installation—is intentionally deferred until after `makepkg` has completed its initial setup phase. Therefore, `makepkg --printsrcinfo` poses no security risk in this context.
</details>
